title: Sean McVay on defending against the Bills’ offense, decision-making, Week 5 injury report & more
headline: Rams look mostly healthy for Monday night against Buffalo: Aaron Donald and Colby Parkinson are good to go, and only Quentin Lake is listed as questionable. A player coming off knee surgery likely won't have his return clock started next week.
summary: McVay said Aaron Donald did not practice but is fine and has no injury designation for the game. Quentin Lake is the only Ram listed as questionable, and McVay said he feels good and is trending in the right direction. A reporter asked about Colby Parkinson and another player named "Jalen", and McVay said both are good to go. McVay did not name the player recovering from knee surgery. He said the surgery went well and the timeline is week to week, but it's more likely the team does not start his clock next week. He stressed the difference between return to play and return to performance, and said the player needs to hit benchmarks and do football activities before the team talks about him playing. He praised Josh Allen as a smarter, more rhythm-based passer who beats defenses with his arm and legs, and called him very special and troublesome to defend. The rest of the session covered the analytics debate on going for two when down 14. McVay said he would kick the extra point and decide on the next possession. He added that game flow, personnel and the people playing matter alongside analytics.

topics.detail: McVay praised Allen's growth in timing, rhythm, reading coverage and using all five eligible receivers, plus his off-schedule ability. He called him a very special and troublesome player to defend and said the team is excited for the challenge.

McVay did not name the player, but described a week-to-week recovery with a likely delay in starting his return clock. He said the player's limited training camp practice came from knee irritation that the surgery fixed, which should speed up his ramp-up. He wants the player doing football drills before a return.

McVay would kick the extra point when down 14 and decide on a two-point try later. He said analytics are a major input but not the only one, alongside game flow, matchups and personnel. He credited Dan Shamash for communication in those moments.
McVay offered condolences and praised Ditka's toughness, leadership and legacy, noting he never knew him personally.
